result.title: Should Pseudo-Labels Share Mini-Batches with Labeled Examples? Semi-Supervised Continual Active Learning with Limited Training Cost
result.summary: Active learning (AL) reduces annotation by querying informative examples. Continual active learning (CAL) also cuts the training cost, the total number of gradient steps, by training one model across AL rounds with a fixed number of mini-batch steps per round. Pseudo-labels add supervision without annotation, but they increase training cost. In CAL, where every round trains on a fixed number of mini-batches, whether and how pseudo-labeled examples should share these mini-batches with labeled examples is therefore open. We provide the first formalization of this problem as two decisions after each query, namely (i) which unlabeled examples should enter training with a pseudo-label and (ii) what share of each mini-batch they should take. Our method, semi-supervised continual active learning (SSCAL), works with any acquisition function. It admits pseudo-labels based on distances from unlabeled examples to labeled neighbors, caps their share, and reweights the loss on labeled examples to keep their expected gradient contribution unchanged. On frozen embeddings, its pseudo-labeler updates incrementally without extra model forward passes. Across two audio datasets, two frozen encoders, six acquisition functions and ten seeds, SSCAL ranks first on average among four protocols with equal training steps, answering the question affirmatively.

AI.brief_summary: 论文把半监督持续主动学习形式化为每轮查询后的两个决策——哪些无标签样本带伪标签进入训练、每个 mini-batch 中占多大比例，提出 SSCAL：基于冻结嵌入到有标签邻居的距离生成伪标签、限制其占比并对有标签样本损失重加权以保持期望梯度贡献，在音频数据上以相同训练步数比较多种取得函数。
AI.relevance_reason: 在固定梯度步数预算下决定监督来源与份额、并用重加权保持贡献不变，可能为 LVR/VLM 推理训练中的监督预算分配与「计算/信息价值」评价提供类比线索，但其视觉推理适用性需核查。
